investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T14:36:47Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a created agent, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable. This is an eval-layer failure caused by a backend quota enforcement response; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval run.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api Swarm backend rejected the eval's agent creation request with HTTP 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1339) never succeeded, the probe returned the raw 409 error message instead of evidence, causing all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to fail with the identical message. The quota limit on the eval's org or service account has been reached, preventing any new remote agent from being provisioned by the probe.

possibleCauses: Primary — Eval service account or org has accumulated 100 remote agents (the stated quota limit) from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up, causing every new POST /api/agents to be rejected with 409. This is the most direct reading of the error message.

Secondary — A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted inside withCleanup before the cleanup callback could delete the probe agent, leaving a leaked agent that counts against the quota. Repeated leaks across runs would accumulate toward the limit.
Tertiary — The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the backend (e.g., a Swarm configuration change), causing an org that was previously under quota to now be over it.

Low-confidence hypothesis — Commit 5a0475f (suspect-change.5a0475f, confidence: low) touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-observability-repair.yml; if it changed how the observability workflow provisions or cleans up agents it could have contributed to agent leakage, but the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and no eval-runner source changes are confirmed in the diff, so this remains unproven.

investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 311 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. possibleCauses: Most likely — The aura-observability GitHub Actions workflow was delayed, skipped, or failed silently, causing the snapshot to go unpublished for more than 300 minutes. The snapshot URL is a GitHub Pages static file, so a missed or failed workflow run would leave the previous file in place with an advancing age.

Possible — Commit 5a0475f ('fix(observability): stabilize status freshness signals', committed 2026-06-16T14:26:04Z, ~10 minutes before the eval) touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and .github/workflows/aura-observability-repair.yml. Least likely — The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) has a clock or timezone offset bug that inflates the reported age. This is unlikely because generatedAtPresent=true passed, indicating the runner did find a generatedAt timestamp in the payload.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes 311 > max 300)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 311 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is a localized eval failure against the snapshot freshness assertion; all three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming no broader website outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot (status.json) did not run within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 11 minutes past its freshness deadline when the eval executed at 2026-06-16T14:36:54Z, meaning the last successful workflow publish occurred approximately at or before 2026-06-16T09:25Z. The eval contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 410 asserts snapshotAgeMinutes max 300; the live evidence value was 311 (failed-check.evidence). No evidence of a user-facing outage is present; the check is marked required=false with statusImpact=informational (source.infra/evals/status/features.json:361).
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 311' — the sole violated assertion in the contract.
failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=311, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — all other assertions passed; only the age bound was breached.
source.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:400 (line 410): assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } is the exact contract clause that failed.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:361: check config shows required=false, statusImpact=informational, staleAfterMinutes=360 — the registry staleAfterMinutes (360) is looser than the contract max (300), indicating the contract is the binding freshness gate.
sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 and valid app shells — no shared dependency failure, no broader website outage.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=54 — the eval itself completed normally; the failure is data-staleness, not a network or runner error.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1622-1627: runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload — the runner executed correctly and the age value reflects the actual published file timestamp.
possibleCauses: Most likely — The aura-observability GitHub Actions workflow was delayed, skipped, or failed silently, causing the snapshot to go unpublished for more than 300 minutes. The snapshot URL is a GitHub Pages static file, so a missed or failed workflow run would leave the previous file in place with an advancing age.

Possible — Commit 5a0475f ('fix(observability): stabilize status freshness signals', committed 2026-06-16T14:26:04Z, ~10 minutes before the eval) touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and .github/workflows/aura-observability-repair.yml. If this commit altered the workflow schedule, trigger conditions, or publish step, it could have disrupted the normal cadence. This is a low-confidence hypothesis (suspect-change.5a0475f) because the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list does not include the eval source files and no diff content is available.
Less likely — A GitHub Actions runner quota, concurrency limit, or Pages deployment throttle caused the workflow to queue and not complete within the window, without the workflow itself failing.

Least likely — The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) has a clock or timezone offset bug that inflates the reported age. This is unlikely because generatedAtPresent=true passed, indicating the runner did find a generatedAt timestamp in the payload.
